shots.title: Accept --sprint N and a bare positional sprint number in slope review, not only --sprint=N (#689)
shots.notes: The trigger was one line in src/cli/index.ts: sprintArg matched only args starting with '--sprint=', so with `--sprint 259` the flag was skipped and 259 became the first non-dash arg, i.e. the path — hence 'Failed to parse <cwd>/259'. Extracted parseReviewArgs into review.ts so the parsing is unit-testable without running the CLI; it consumes a space-separated flag value and treats a bare S?N(.N) positional as a selector, leaving real paths alone.

shots.title: Tolerate a missing tickets key at the validateRoadmap API boundary instead of throwing (#685)

hazards.description: The issue reported this as a CLI crash, but the CLI path was already fixed: parseRoadmap normalizes `tickets ?? []` (commit 400b422, fix(S147-533)). Only direct API callers still threw. Verifying against the current build before writing code changed the scope from a hunt across four commands to one guard clause.

shots.notes: validateRoadmap shallow-clones the roadmap when any sprint lacks a tickets array, so a missing key behaves exactly like an explicit [] — the option the issue preferred, and the one that matches what the CLI already did. Deliberately does NOT emit an extra error: parseRoadmap fills the key in first, so an error here would fire only for API callers and make the two paths disagree. The caller's object is left untouched.

shots.title: Extend the shipped-commit metadata allowlist to the modular docs/roadmap sources (#686)
shots.notes: Found while verifying #686, not in the issue: isSlopeMetadataPath allowlisted docs/backlog/roadmap.json but not docs/roadmap/**.yaml, which is where this project now authors its roadmap. A conventional-commit implementation type touching only phase YAML would still have counted as shipping. The subject-level filters (isPlanningOnlyBareReference, range detection) already caught every subject in the issue, so this was the remaining file-level hole.

shots.title: Lock the verified-fixed signal regressions with tests so #684/#686/#688/#690 can close (#684)
shots.notes: tests/core/issue-regressions.test.ts pins the reported SYMPTOM of each issue rather than the implementation: #684's exact scorecard shape renders 100% (3/3) and never '(0/0)'; every commit subject quoted in #686 and #690 extracts to an empty set while real feat(S80)/(S80-2) commits still ship; #688's staleness check reports OK against the count the map itself writes. These four were fixed in earlier sprints with no test holding the symptom, so they could have regressed silently.

bunker_locations: src/cli/index.ts flag parsing is per-command and ad hoc: several commands match only the '--flag=value' spelling, so the space-separated form silently falls through to a positional. Worth auditing the other commands for the same gap.

Verify a reported bug against the current build before scoping work on it. Four of the eight open issues were already fixed and one was half-fixed; triaging from issue text alone would have produced three unnecessary sprints.
notes: Closes the Phase 62 residue. #689 and #685 were both half-fixed already — #689's --help and equals form worked, #685's CLI path was safe — so the live surface was much smaller than filed, and the sprint spent its remaining budget on the regression tests that let #684, #686, #688 and #690 close honestly. Full suite green (4320 passed), typecheck clean, map regenerated.
